I'll build the water volume as a union of axis-aligned boxes (three passes along X, pitch 7 mm = 4 wide + 3 metal, 5 mm deep), then mesh with snappyHexMesh on a 1 mm background grid.

```python
import subprocess, os
from build123d import *

mm = 1e-3
# --- parameters (mm, converted at the end) ---
PL, PW, PH = 60.0, 40.0, 8.0      # plate 60 x 40 x 8
CW, CD     = 4.0, 5.0             # channel width, depth
RIB        = 3.0                  # metal between passes
EDGE       = 2.0                  # metal between U-turn outer wall and plate edge
ZC0, ZC1   = PH - CD, PH          # channel milled from top: z 3 -> 8

pitch = CW + RIB                  # 7
yc = [PW/2 - pitch, PW/2, PW/2 + pitch]   # pass centrelines: 13, 20, 27
xt_r = PL - EDGE - CW/2           # right turn centre x = 56
xt_l = EDGE + CW/2                # left  turn centre x = 4

def box(x0, x1, y0, y1):
    return Pos((x0+x1)/2, (y0+y1)/2, (ZC0+ZC1)/2) * Box(x1-x0, y1-y0, CD)

leg1  = box(0.0,        xt_r+CW/2, yc[0]-CW/2, yc[0]+CW/2)   # inlet at x=0
turn1 = box(xt_r-CW/2,  xt_r+CW/2, yc[0]-CW/2, yc[1]+CW/2)
leg2  = box(xt_l-CW/2,  xt_r+CW/2, yc[1]-CW/2, yc[1]+CW/2)
turn2 = box(xt_l-CW/2,  xt_l+CW/2, yc[1]-CW/2, yc[2]+CW/2)
leg3  = box(xt_l-CW/2,  PL,        yc[2]-CW/2, yc[2]+CW/2)   # outlet at x=PL

fluid_mm = leg1 + turn1 + leg2 + turn2 + leg3
print("bbox mm:", fluid_mm.bounding_box())
print("volume mm^3:", fluid_mm.volume)
print("pass centres y:", yc, " rib gap:", (yc[1]-CW/2)-(yc[0]+CW/2))
```
Volume 3560 mm³ = centreline 178 mm × 20 mm² exactly, rib gap 3.0 mm. Now scale to metres, split the authored inlet/outlet planes off, export patch STLs, and render.
Inlet (0, 13, 5.5) and outlet (60, 27, 5.5), each 20 mm² = 4×5. Export the three patch STLs and render.
Mesher rejects open face sheets; I'll tessellate faces myself and write ASCII STL per patch.
Walls open only at the two ends (8 free edges), as expected. Render to look at it.
Geometry looks right. Now a coarse snappyHexMesh case: 1 mm background grid, no refinement.
Coarse mesh is good (volume 3.56002e-6 m³ vs exact 3.56e-6). Now refine to 0.5 mm cells (8×10 across the 4×5 mm channel).
Let me verify the inlet/outlet patch areas from the mesh itself and render a slice.

Water-side volume built and meshed.

```python
# summary cell (no-op)
print("done")
```

What I built: the fluid volume of a serpentine channel milled 5 mm deep into the top of a 60×40×8 mm plate — three passes along X on 7 mm pitch (4 mm channel + 3 mm rib, measured rib gap = 3.000 mm), U-turns 2 mm clear of the plate edges, inlet at x = 0 (y = 13, z 3–8) and outlet at x = 60 (y = 27), both open ends of the channel. Metres throughout (authored in mm, scaled once by 1e-3).

Numbers measured against the request: bbox of fluid 0–60 × 11–29 × 3–8 mm, all inside the 60×40×8 plate; volume 3560.0 mm³ = 178 mm centreline × 20 mm² exactly; meshed volume 3.55994e-6 m³ (−0.002 %); inlet and outlet patch areas both exactly 20.000 mm² = 4×5 mm; wall wetted area 3203.7 mm² ≈ 18 mm perimeter × 178 mm.

Mesh: 0.5 mm background grid + snappyHexMesh, 27 110 cells (8×10 cells across the channel), 26 370 hexes, patches `walls` (wall), `inlet`, `outlet`. checkMesh: Mesh OK, max non-orthogonality 40.2 (avg 5.1), max skewness 1.69, max aspect ratio 10.1.

Not checked / accepted: snapping leaves the wall surface up to ~30 µm below the nominal z = 3 mm floor (0.6 % of depth) at a few turn corners; no boundary layers were added (addLayers false), and the solid aluminium side was not meshed, as requested.
